allow_unverified_integration_results.description:
A dangerous bypass, off by default. On, results from the service's integration endpoints, reads and
writes, never count as a patient record for the output checker's unverified-caller check, so the agent may
read them back to any caller, verified or not. Writes are still held to everything else, the platform's own
patient reads still refuse until the caller verifies, and data queries and skills still count. Never on
beside `caller_verification_endpoint_id`. Only a platform admin (`platform:admin`) turns it on; turning it
off needs `Service.update`. Every change is audited.
allow_unverified_integration_results.title: Allow Unverified Integration Results

caller_verification_endpoint_id.description:
The integration endpoint that verifies this service's callers, on a service with
`platform_caller_verification` and `allow_unverified_integration_results` false. The endpoint has to
be one of this workspace's, declare `declarations.verifies`, and never wait for approval under its
integration's `approval_policy`. A successful call verifies the caller as the one patient its response
names there, once per conversation. The reads of that integration that declare the patient they read
refuse until then, and then run only for that patient, and the agent may share what they return.
Naming one needs `Service.update`.

crisis statement keeps the call open in either.

platform_caller_verification.description:
Whether the platform verifies a caller who may match a patient record by full name and date of
birth. Off, the agent never asks a caller to verify, and every platform tool that reads a patient
record refuses. The service's integration tools run either way, unless one of them verifies its
callers (`caller_verification_endpoint_id`).

caller_id.description: Simulated caller phone number used to resolve patient context when `entity_id` is not provided (or does not match a row). entity_id.description: Optional world entity UUID to bind caller context directly. Precedence rules: (1) when this resolves to a world entity in the workspace, it WINS — `caller_id` is not used for identity resolution, and the resolution provenance is `entity_id_lookup`; (2) when this is a well-formed UUID with no matching entity (stale, deleted, wrong workspace), the session falls back to phone lookup against `caller_id` (provenance `phone_lookup`) — no error is raised, the sim is survivable; (3) malformed UUIDs are rejected with HTTP 422 before the session starts. The supplied `caller_id` is still recorded on the active call and surfaced in the greeting metadata in case (1).

GraphQLSuccess.description:
The request is a GraphQL mutation, and every mutation payload holds something other than null
past its user errors. Top-level ``errors`` in an answer with no ``data`` are a request that never
ran. Beside ``data`` they're read by their ``path``: one at the mutation's own field, with that
field null, is its resolver refusing, and one below it came after the write, so a payload that
still holds its result wrote. A request that never ran, or a resolver that refused, is a write
that didn't happen. Any other answer with errors leaves the outcome unknown, such as a payload
GraphQL nulled on the way up, or an error with no path beside ``data``. So does a null ``data`` in
a document of more than one mutation: they run in order, and the null hides what the ones before
the failing one did.

OpenerFailureResponse.description:
The body of a failed outbound opener.

``detail`` says what failed. ``outcome``, ``reason`` and ``conversation_id`` say what happened to the
opener's message and where, when the platform has a report of it; a failure it has none of carries
``detail`` alone.

conversation_id.description:
The conversation the opener ran in, or null when none had been created. Absent when the platform has no
report of the opener.
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

outcome.description:
What came of the opener's send. ``delivered``: the channel took the message, and a later step failed.
``unknown``: the send failed after the request may have reached the channel, so the message may have gone
out. ``rejected``: the channel refused the message, so it did not go out. ``not_sent``: the agent produced
no message to send. ``error``: the run failed before any send began. Absent when the platform has no report
of the opener.
outcome.title: Outcome

reason.description:
Why the opener ended as it did. A failed send is named by how it failed: ``timeout``, ``connection``,
``http_4xx``, ``http_5xx`` or ``error``. A refused message is ``opted_out`` (the recipient opted out) or
``invalid_content``. A run that sent nothing is ``no_opener`` (the agent produced no message),
``llm_timeout`` (the model did not answer in time) or ``lease_contended`` (another run held the
conversation). A failure in the run is ``session_init``, ``persist`` or ``agent_error``. ``unanswered``:
the agent runtime gave no answer. Null when the send went out and nothing failed after it. Absent when the
platform has no report of the opener.
reason.title: Reason

the instant the tool is dispatched, before the 15s blocking floor elapses, so a
subscribed client shows progress immediately instead of waiting out the floor in
silence (PLA-986). Emitted for tools that route through the background/floor-promoted
dispatch paths (companion skills and ``execution="background"`` tools) — the ones

matching the eventual ``TextBackgroundResultEvent`` (and the next-turn drained card
from ``build_background_completion_effect``), so a client collapses started → result

conversation UUID (non-web channels route by a composite key and deliver via their own
transport).

Answers a ``wait_for_final`` wait collected still come back. ``null`` (default) inherits the channel policy. Ignored with ``poll=true`` (422).

wait_for_final.description: Synchronous callers only: when a turn hands work to a background tool (``background_pending``), await this turn's answer inline instead of returning the acknowledgement immediately. The turn and the wait share one budget of about 170 seconds, so give the request a client timeout of at least 180 seconds. The response carries the answers the turn's background work commits, in order, in place of the acknowledgement, so a tool that hands off to another returns both messages; ``background_pending=false`` means ``output`` is the turn's whole answer. Otherwise (time ran out, or an earlier turn's answer is still waiting to be collected) it returns what arrived, or the acknowledgement, with ``background_pending=true``; collect the rest with ``poll=true``, and poll before sending the next turn. Send an ``Idempotency-Key`` with every waiting turn: if your own timeout fires or the connection drops first, retry with the same key, and the retry returns the answers the turn already collected instead of running it again. ``null`` (default) inherits the channel policy (web = do not wait). task, so ``output`` is NOT the final answer — the definitive assistant answer is
produced later, out-of-band. Under delivery protocol v2, collect it by re-issuing
``POST …/turns`` with ``poll=true`` (a no-message, receipt-backed claim), render or
durably persist the returned answer, then acknowledge its exact delivery receipt.
This is the per-conversation delivery contract — see
the web-integration paved path. (``GET /v1/{workspace_id}/events/stream?conversation_id=``
mirrors this activity as ``text.tool_started`` / ``text.background_result`` /
``text.agent_message`` for a view watching this one conversation, but is not the
per-chat delivery path. The stream without ``conversation_id`` carries none of it.) A
client that treats a ``background_pending=true`` turn as complete without polling and
acknowledging will miss the final answer.

A new workspace data query: a SQL template and the parameters it declares.

The SQL template must be one SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE statement that calls only built-in
functions which run no SQL text and change no session state. Its `:name` placeholders and the declared
parameters must be the same set of names: each placeholder is declared, and each declared parameter appears
in the template. A parameter's `default`, when set, must be of its declared `type`. A body that breaks any
of these rules returns 422.

post.description: Initiate an outbound voice call from a workspace phone number, chosen for the given use_case_id. Send an idempotency_key so a retry doesn't place a second call. After a 502, 503 or 504, retry with the same key and the same request: while the first attempt is still being placed the retry gets 409, once that call is placed it gets the call's response, and if the attempt placed nothing it places the call. A 503 may carry Retry-After: wait that long first. A 422 is final: the call was refused (for example an invalid number), or the use case's service runs on gpt_realtime, which doesn't take system_prompt, goal or outbound_task_entity_id, so place the call without them. A 500 reporting refused platform credentials requires a configuration fix before retrying. Other 500 errors may be transient; the call may still be placed, so reuse the same idempotency_key if retrying.
